subject: Early termination fee trigger and renewal grace exceptions — MSA/Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Acme redlines — early termination fee trigger + renewal grace exceptions (MSA / OF)

Team,

Acme sent back the order form with two items we need to resolve before we can push the signature: (1) a request to carve out pilots and low-TCV customers from the early termination fee (ETF) and (2) asks for a wide "renewal grace" provision that effectively extends auto-renew notice windows for select SKUs. I've attached the redlines and the MSA extract for the TfC (termination for convenience) clause.

Quick facts: deal HS-32458 is $420k ARR (first-year TCV ~$500k), pilot component is $25k, customer asks that pilots and any single-product subscriptions < $75k be exempt from ETF. They also want an 30-day rolling renewal-cure window that would override our standard 60-day notice for the Order Form.

What I need from you by EOD Tuesday (11/03):
- Legal (Laura + Kimberly) — recommended position on ETF carveout thresholds and whether we can accept a pilot carveout limited to proof-of-concept (timeboxed + written acceptance). Also need redline language we can send back (suggested alternatives).
- Sales (Aditya) — confirm whether we can offer a one-time concession (e.g., waive ETF for pilot only) in exchange for a commitment to a 12-month minimum on conversion. Is TM/Finance comfortable with a $75k floor?

Suggested starting positions (feel free to push back):
- ETF applies pro rata based on remaining committed months; waive ETF for pilots only if pilot < $30k and pilot has signed acceptance criteria;
- Keep standard auto-renew notice at 60 days; offer a one-time 30-day grace in writing for a single renewal cycle only (not evergreen);

Attachments: OrderForm_Acme_v3_redline.pdf (pdf), MSA_excerpt_TfC_clause.txt (txt)

I'll consolidate and draft a response for Acme.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme redlines — early termination fee trigger + renewal grace exceptions (MSA / OF)

Sergio —

Thanks for the summary and the docs. High level thoughts:
- ETF carveout: I'm reluctant to give a blanket exemption < $75k. That creates a litmus test that customers will try to game. Recommend: allow an exception only for timeboxed pilots <= $30k with explicit acceptance criteria and a signed pilot SOW. For conversions, require a 12-month commitment to remove the carveout.
- ETF scale: propose a scaled ETF (months remaining / total committed months * remaining fees) capped at 6 months of revenue. That gives us predictability and aligns with our revenue exposure.
- Renewal grace: we should not give a perpetual 30-day override. If we can offer a one-time 30-day courtesy for the first renewal only (documented as an amendment to the Order Form), that's ok. Anything longer or evergreen is a no.
- Alternative language suggestion: I'll draft a short paragraph to insert into the Order Form that captures the pilot carveout conditions and the one-time grace.

One operational note: HubSpot deal HS-32458 shows pilot as a distinct line item — if Sales wants the pilot carveout we should require separate line items and a signed pilot acceptance doc to be attached to the OF.

I'll prepare redline text in LEG-198 and paste it here by lunchtime.

-K

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Acme redlines — early termination fee trigger + renewal grace exceptions (MSA / OF)

Short — Sales is okay to accept the pilot carveout under the conditions Kimberly outlined (<= $30k, signed acceptance, one-time waiver on conversion to follow-on contract only if 12-month minimum). Finance pushed back on a $75k floor; they'd prefer a strict pilot-only carveout. If Legal can provide language we can sign off on, I'll loop in RevOps to make sure billing is set to enforce the pilot separation.

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Order Form v3 — follow-up on TfC / renewal windows

Priya —

Thanks for sending the redlines. We reviewed internally and want to propose a narrow compromise that preserves both parties' commercial certainty and avoids open-ended exemptions. High-level proposal:

1) Pilot carveout: Redwood will waive the ETF for a timeboxed pilot not to exceed $30,000 TCV provided the pilot is documented with acceptance criteria and a signed pilot SOW attached to the Order Form. If the customer converts the pilot to a full paid subscription, Redwood will require a 12-month minimum term for that converted subscription; otherwise ETF applies.

2) Renewal notice/grace: We cannot accept a perpetual reduction to the standard 60-day termination notice. However, as a one-time concession we will accept a single 30-day notice for the next renewal cycle only, documented as an amendment to the Order Form. This concession is not transferable and will not apply to subsequent renewals.

3) ETF calculation: ETF will be calculated pro rata based on remaining committed months, capped at 6 months of recurring charges.

If Acme is comfortable with this framework we'll provide redline language within 24 hours and circulate a final OF for signature. If you'd like to propose alternative wording, please share and we'll review with Legal.

Available for a short sync today if helpful — suggest a 20-min call at 2pm PT.

Best,
Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme.io>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.io>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form v3 — follow-up on TfC / renewal windows

Sergio —

Appreciate the quick response and the willingness to find a compromise. We're generally aligned on the pilot carveout but need the pilot threshold to be $50k (their Procurement group asked us to push for a slightly larger pilot band). They also want the renewal grace to apply to any product line that has been inactive for >180 days (they called it a "dormant SKU" exception) — that one is important for their PMs.

From Legal: they asked for alternate wording that is simpler to operate against (we've pasted their suggested clause below). Please review and let us know if we can accept the alternate language or provide a redline. If you prefer, we can put Acme Legal and your counsel on a 30-min call tomorrow to hammer this out.

--- forwarded message ---
From: Acme Legal <legal@acme.io>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:40:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed alternate wording for pilot carveout and renewal grace
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme.io>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Proposed clause (excerpt):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer may elect to exclude timeboxed pilot programs from any early termination fee provided that (i) the pilot is expressly identified in the Order Form, (ii) pilot acceptance criteria and success metrics are agreed in writing, and (iii) Customer converts the pilot to paid service within 90 days of completion to avoid subsequent fee exposure. For any product line where Customer has not transacted or used the Service for a period greater than 180 days, Customer may request a single 30-day reduction to the standard notice period for the next renewal only. Such requests shall be submitted in writing and are subject to Redwood's approval."

They note that the 90-day conversion window narrows risk to Acme and the 180-day dormant-SKU carveout addresses their internal product cycles.

Can your Legal team take a look at the proposed excerpt and advise whether Redwood can accept as-is or propose edits? If your team is ok with a small concession on pilot size to $50k in exchange for the 90-day conversion window and the non-transferable, one-time dormant-SKU exception, we'll move quickly.

Thanks — will await your suggested redline.

Best,
Priya
Priya Desai
Senior Procurement Lead | Acme, Inc.
